problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the points $C(1,1,1)$ and $D(-3,2,4)$, and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨0,1,1⟩.$
worked_solution:
First, we need to find two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other). We already have one vector $v=⟨0,1,1⟩.$ Let's also use the displacement vector $\overset{\to }{CD}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{CD} & =⟨-3,2,4⟩-⟨1,1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,1,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if we consider the position vector $c=⟨1,1,1⟩$ of the point $C,$ then the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =c+sv+t\overset{\to }{CD} \\ r & =⟨1,1,1⟩+s⟨0,1,1⟩+t⟨-4,1,3⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
